title: Deterministic or stochastic trend: detrend or difference?

explain.prompt: US diesel demand and the Brent price both trend. Using `adf_p_c`, `adf_p_ct`, `std_detrended` and `std_differenced`, explain in 5–7 sentences why the right transformation differs. What would go wrong if you differenced demand, or detrended Brent? Why is the seasonal profile removed first?
rubric: Demand (after removing the seasonal profile): ADF with a constant does not reject (p ≈ 0.97) but with constant + trend rejects (p < 0.001) → a deterministic trend (≈ +12.9 kb/d per year): trend-stationary, shocks fade → detrend.
Brent monthly average 2012–2019: neither 'c' (p ≈ 0.34) nor 'ct' (p ≈ 0.87) rejects → stochastic trend, permanent shocks → difference (returns).
Differencing a trend-stationary series over-differences: the dispersion rises (≈ 15.6 vs ≈ 11.6 kb/d) and the level information is thrown away.
Detrending a random walk leaves a residual that still wanders (≈ 18.3 vs ≈ 4.2 USD/bbl for monthly changes): a fitted line on Brent is an artefact of the sample.

Seasonality first: a winter-peaking profile (≈ 79 kb/d peak to trough) would otherwise distort the tests; it is estimated on the detrended series so that later months are not credited with more trend.
The decision uses the chart and the economics too: consumption follows activity along a path; a price has no deterministic anchor.
